title: ReviewDebt: a practical framework for scoring every pull request — Sachin Gupta, Ebay
talk_summary: Sachin Gupta argues that AI coding agents create 'review debt' — code produced faster than humans can review and trust — and proposes a deterministic, LLM-free scoring framework of five signal families (size/coupling, test evidence gap, ownership spread, AI authorship indicators, evidence/rationale gap) that produces a 0-100 review-burden score with structured reviewer/author advice. He shows a scan of 524 public PRs where volume, not AI authorship, drove review burden, and recommends backfilling scores over past PRs, surfacing scores as non-blocking PR comments, and tracking the weekly slope per team.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic PR review-burden scoring (no LLM judge)
takeaways.what_they_do: Compute a 0-100 score from 10 deterministic checks across five signal families (net lines/files/coupling, test-lines/prod-lines ratio, distinct code-owner teams touched, AI-authorship markers like co-authored footers and branch prefixes, and PR-body/commit-message rationale completeness), then emit structured reviewer-focus and author-next-action lists.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every check is computable from a pull request and its repository. No, we don't need any language model.
takeaways.numbers: 524 PRs scanned; 228 senior reviewer hours cumulative; one PR estimated at 5,036 minutes (84 hours) review effort; AI indicators fired on 5-20% of PRs weekly

takeaways.technique: Structured advice output, not just a score
takeaways.what_they_do: The scanner emits a fired-checks list, a reviewer-focus list telling the reviewer what to do next, and an author-next-action list telling the author how to lower the score; healthy PRs produce an almost empty report to avoid noise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The score alone is useful. The structured advice is what actually moves the team behavior.

takeaways.technique: Evidence/rationale gap check on PR bodies
takeaways.what_they_do: Score whether the PR explains the why (symptom, diagnosis, change, benchmark link) versus just the what (short body, 'updates' commit message); they call this the signal that destroys reviewability fastest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Does the PR explain the why or just the what?

takeaways.technique: Test-evidence-gap ratio plus 'asserts what should be, not what is'
takeaways.what_they_do: Compute test lines added divided by production lines added per PR as a cheap proxy, while explicitly acknowledging the ratio misses quality — agents write tests that lock in current behavior including bugs, so a human must confirm tests assert intended behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They generate a lot of test. But these test basically assert what the code is doing... They lock in the behavior including the bugs.

takeaways.technique: Ownership-spread check to cap cross-team PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: Count distinct code-owner teams whose files appear in the diff; sprawling PRs need multiple approvals in multiple contexts, and coordination overhead exceeds the agent's typing savings.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The agent gave you three hours of typing. You spend those three hours by multi-party reviewer attention.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the scorer backwards over the last 200 merged PRs to calibrate weights against gut feel, set a threshold (e.g., 50) above which the author must comment, post the score as a non-blocking PR comment, and track the weekly slope per team as the leading indicator.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Run it backwards over the last 200 PRs that have been merged in your company. Calibrate the weights against your team's actual reviewer experience.
takeaways.numbers: Suggested threshold 50; bands 0-24 low, 25-49 normal, 50-74 needs evidence, 75+ split/request context
